reviews.review:
100 nya is a deliberately minimal puzzle game that takes inspiration from one of the most recognizable movement rules in chess and turns it into a focused test of planning. Developed and published by .M.Y.W., the game revolves around moving across a board using the same L-shaped pattern as a chess knight. The objective is straightforward: work toward reaching 100 while carefully considering where each move will leave you. There is very little unnecessary decoration surrounding this idea, making the experience primarily about logic, positioning, and thinking several moves ahead.

The simplicity of the rules makes the game immediately understandable, but successfully navigating the board is considerably more demanding than the premise initially suggests. Knight movement creates unusual routes because the player cannot simply travel toward the next desirable position in a straight line. Every choice changes the available possibilities that follow, and careless movement can eventually leave the player without a useful route. This gives the puzzle a strategic quality where early decisions can have consequences much later in an attempt.

Much of the satisfaction comes from gradually recognizing movement patterns. An unsuccessful run is not necessarily wasted because it can reveal where a particular route becomes problematic. Starting again with that knowledge allows the player to experiment with a different sequence and potentially improve the result. The game consequently rewards patience and observation more than quick reflexes. Players who enjoy solving mathematical puzzles, chess problems, route-planning challenges, or optimization exercises are the audience most likely to appreciate what it offers.

Replayability is based primarily on finding different approaches rather than receiving large quantities of new content. The basic mechanics remain consistent, so repeated attempts depend heavily on the player's willingness to master the central puzzle. There is an appealing purity to this design because the game does not constantly interrupt its logic challenge with unrelated mechanics. On the other hand, this also means that anyone expecting a substantial campaign, evolving mechanics, elaborate progression, or significant narrative content may find the experience too limited.

The presentation follows the same minimalist philosophy. Visuals mainly exist to communicate the board and current situation clearly rather than impress through elaborate artwork or animation. This functional approach suits the gameplay because the player needs to concentrate on positions and possible moves. The technical requirements are correspondingly modest, making this the kind of small puzzle game that does not need powerful PC hardware to deliver its intended experience.

Another positive aspect is how accessible the core concept can be. Familiarity with chess is useful because players will immediately understand the knight's movement, but extensive knowledge of chess strategy is unnecessary. The game isolates that single movement rule and builds its challenge around it. Newcomers can therefore understand what they are supposed to do quickly, while more methodical puzzle enthusiasts can spend additional time attempting to discover increasingly effective routes.

Its greatest weakness is ultimately inseparable from its identity. There simply is not a great deal of mechanical variety. Once the player understands the rules and general structure, the long-term appeal depends almost entirely on enjoying repeated logical experimentation. There are no complex characters, cinematic sequences, enormous environments, or sophisticated progression systems providing additional motivation. This makes it better suited to shorter puzzle sessions than to players seeking a large, content-heavy experience.

Steam Deck compatibility should currently be regarded as Unknown or Unverified rather than officially Verified or Playable. Its lightweight nature and straightforward puzzle design may make it seem like a natural candidate for handheld play, but the absence of an official compatibility classification means a completely trouble-free Steam Deck experience should not be assumed. Players using a Deck may need to experiment with controls or compatibility settings depending on their configuration.

Overall, 100 nya is a small and specialized logic game that understands exactly what type of experience it wants to provide. Its chess-knight movement creates a surprisingly thoughtful challenge from a very small collection of rules, and learning how to avoid trapping yourself provides the main sense of progression. The limited amount of variety prevents it from becoming an essential puzzle title, but players attracted to minimalist brain teasers can still find worthwhile entertainment in mastering its movement system. It is best approached as a compact digital logic exercise rather than a conventional adventure or strategy game.

Rating: 6/10
